takeaway: The caval opening at T8 lies in the central tendon. In inspiration the diaphragm contracts and the inferior vena cava dilates, helping blood return to the heart.

question.text: Which statement regarding the apertures of the diaphragm is correct?
question.say: Which statement regarding the apertures of the diaphragm is correct?

answer.text: During inspiration the inferior vena cava dilates facilitating blood flow to the heart.
answer.say: During inspiration the inferior vena cava dilates, facilitating blood flow to the heart.

lines.text: The diaphragm is a dome of muscle with a central tendon in the middle.
The caval opening is at the level of T8, in that central tendon, to the right of the midline.
lines.say: The caval opening is at the level of T eight, in that central tendon, to the right of the midline.

lines.text: The inferior vena cava passes through it, with terminal branches of the right phrenic nerve.
When you breathe in, the diaphragm contracts and flattens.
That makes the inferior vena cava dilate, which helps blood flow back to the heart.
So this is the correct statement.
